name: Abercrombie
summary: Near Raven Hill Cemetery, Abercrombie asks travelers for help from his shack in western Duskwood. He seems a feeble, eccentric hermit, plagued by the horrors of the woods. He sends sympathetic travelers to Darkshire for peculiar reagents and supplies.

sections.title: The Recluse of Raven Hill
sections.body: Abercrombie lives in a dilapidated shack near Raven Hill Cemetery, where Duskwood's decay has left him looking like a broken old man. He says he is only trying to survive the terrors of the woods and asks travelers to bring supplies, herbs, and thread from Darkshire. To anyone who does not know the region's history, he seems another unfortunate soul left behind as the province fell into ruin.

sections.title: The Embalmer's Madness
sections.body: Abercrombie once lived in Raven Hill as a respected, kindly alchemist. When his beloved wife, Eliza, died, grief broke his sanity. He turned to forbidden necromantic arts, cut out his own heart, and placed it in Eliza's dead breast to bring her back. The ritual made her a monster with an insatiable hunger for living flesh, and the mad alchemist kept her buried in the cemetery.

sections.title: A Monstrous Deception
sections.body: Abercrombie, known in dark folklore as the Embalmer, nurses a deep, psychotic grudge against Darkshire and its leaders. He sends helpful travelers for ghoul ribs, specialty thread, and caustic brews. Those supplies are the final parts needed to assemble Stitches, a colossal abomination stitched from flesh and built to slaughter the Night Watch and ravage the town.

faq.answer: Abercrombie is a hermit near Raven Hill Cemetery in Duskwood. Once a skilled alchemist, he lost his mind after his wife died and became the necromantic figure known as the Embalmer.

faq.q: Why does Abercrombie want supplies from Darkshire?
faq.answer: Abercrombie says he needs domestic supplies and thread to survive in the wilderness. In truth, he tricks travelers into gathering the parts needed to assemble Stitches, a monstrous abomination.

Eliza was Abercrombie's wife. After her death, he tried to resurrect her with dark magic by placing his own heart in her corpse. She returned as a ravenous undead monster, and he had to keep her buried in Raven Hill Cemetery.

faq.q: What happens when you deliver the Note to the Mayor?
faq.answer: Lord Ello cannot read the Note because it is written in an ancient language, so he asks Sirra Von'Indi to translate it. The translation reveals that Abercrombie has done something unspeakable. Once Ello reads it, the monstrous Stitches lumbers down the road from Raven Hill toward Darkshire.

Abercrombie never explains his hatred of Darkshire. Grief and dark magic drove him mad after his wife's death, and he mockingly calls Mayor Ello Ebonlocke an old friend as he sends his monstrous creation down the road to destroy the town.

faq.q: Is Abercrombie allied with the Scourge?
faq.answer: No. Abercrombie is a lone hermit with no ties to the Lich King's armies.

angles.text: Alliance heroes who help the miserable hermit unknowingly provide the materials for an assault on Darkshire.
As a paladin, you can see in Abercrombie how necromancy's sinister corruption hides beneath the guise of an ordinary townsman seeking charity.
As a warlock, you can see in Abercrombie's sacrifice of his own heart the extreme, self-destructive lengths mortals will go to wield dark magic.
